title: Examples 286 and 288: the simpleMatch lemma is still proved, and fixed-security with it, after the checker's lemma checks were tightened
description: On 2026-11-17 the checker's rule for a lemma (prove --lemmas) was tightened: a lemma's method, and the lemma's own assumption and assertion, may read no static field that is not final, no non-final field or array cell of an object that was there before the call, and not the default locale; and a method proved by induction is held to the write checks. Before, a lemma about a getter proved in the fresh state stood in for a call made after a write (a false proof, reproduced in lib/tests/claims.rs). The only lemmas the examples use are about PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(String, String): examples 286 (proofs/simple-match.contract, Spring 5.3.19) and 288 (6.1.14). Its bytecode reads no field and no array, so the results of 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-16 did not rest on the hole; this job confirms that the tightened checks still prove the lemma (by induction on the pattern's length) and each example's fixed-security claim at its frozen bound, on the same artifacts. The outcomes go to work folders of their own (.work-286/tightened, .work-288/tightened) so the accepted results' files stay as their jobs wrote them. A refusal of the lemma here (reads the static field, reads an array, reads the default locale) would name what the assertion's stream and regex models read, and is then a finding for the engine's owner, not a reason to loosen the check.
expected: exits 0: each prove.py prints the lemma's own ✓ line and verdict: verified (expected verified)

resources.notes: the earlier jobs' frozen steps: 286 about 15 min of a 23 min job with a trial step, 288 22 min; peak 1.4 GiB each. Plus the release build of lib/. Asked 4G, the local runner's limit per job
